title: Injective homology map of a total resolution
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $n$ an integer, and $M^\bullet$ and $A_i^\bullet$ ($i\geq 0$) cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $\cdots\to A_2^\bullet\to A_1^\bullet\to A_0^\bullet\xrightarrow{a}M^\bullet\to0$ be an augmented chain of maps of complexes, exact in every cochain degree. Assume that for every integer $q$ the augmented row $\cdots\to\ker(d_{A_2}^q)\to\ker(d_{A_1}^q)\to\ker(d_{A_0}^q)\to\ker(d_M^q)\to0$ is exact. Form the direct-sum total complex with $\operatorname{Tot}^k=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_i^{k+i}$ and differential equal to the horizontal differential plus $(-1)^i$ times the vertical differential on column $i$. Let $\varepsilon:\operatorname{Tot}\to M^\bullet$ be the augmentation, equal to $a$ on column zero and zero on the other columns. Then the induced map $H^n(\varepsilon)$ is injective, where cohomology means cycles modulo boundaries.

proof.text: Prove horizontal homology exactness by a boundary-lifting diagram chase. For each interior row, lift the next horizontal image of a boundary primitive through the cycle row, subtract its cycle lift, then lift through the term row. Subtract that primitive differential from the original cycle and use cycle exactness. The p=-2 case uses surjectivity of augmented cycles, the p=-3 case uses augmented cycle exactness, and lower columns use the interior cycle rows. At column zero, lift primitives directly by surjectivity on terms. These chases are fully proved as private Lean helpers.

Construct the column-zero inclusion j as a chain map, using vanishing of the positive columns. Its composite with ε is a. Apply the column-zero representative theorem with the exact horizontal homology rows just proved to obtain surjectivity of H(j).

Construct the explicit null-homotopy of K.d(-1,0) composed with j: in degree q the homotopy is the inclusion from bidegree (-1,q) into total degree q-1. The vertical differential has sign -1, so it cancels the source differential. Thus H(K.d(-1,0)) composed with H(j) is zero.

For x in the kernel of H(ε), choose y with H(j)y=x. Then H(a)y=0. The augmented homology exactness already proved lifts y to H(K.X(-1)); the null-homotopy forces x=0. Apply the linear-map zero-kernel criterion for injectivity.

theorem total_resolution_homology_injective
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (K : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (ε : K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⟶ M)
    (a : K.X 0 ⟶ M)
    [∀ i, (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).HasHomology i]
    [∀ i, M.HasHomology i]
    [∀ p q, (K.X p).HasHomology q]
    (n : ℤ)
    (h_positive : ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero (K.X p))
    (h_augmentation_zero : ∀ q : ℤ,
      K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 q q (by simp) ≫ ε.f q = a.f q)
    (h_augmentation : ∀ (p q n : ℤ) (hp : p < 0)
      (h : ComplexShape.π (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (p, q) = n),
      K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q n h ≫ ε.f n = 0)
    (h_exact : ∀ (p q : ℤ), p < -1 →
      Function.Exact
        ((K.d p (p + 1)).f q).hom
        ((K.d (p + 1) (p + 2)).f q).hom)
    (h_exact_zero : ∀ q : ℤ, Function.Exact
      ((K.d (-1) 0).f q).hom (a.f q).hom)
    (h_surjective : ∀ q : ℤ, Function.Surjective
      (a.f q).hom)
    (h_cycles : ∀ (p q : ℤ), p < -1 →
      Function.Exact
        (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap (K.d p (p + 1)) q).hom
        (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap (K.d (p + 1) (p + 2)) q).hom)
    (h_cycles_zero : ∀ q : ℤ, Function.Exact
      (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap (K.d (-1) 0) q).hom
      (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap a q).hom)
    (h_cycles_surjective : ∀ q : ℤ, Function.Surjective
      (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap a q).hom) :
    Function.Injective (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ε n).hom
